lines.text: A hole in a ring tells time.
It is called a ring dial, a small brass sundial.
Many hung from a thumb or from a neck cord.
Sunlight passes through a tiny pinhole in the ring.
A dot of light lands on an hour scale inside the ring.
The light itself shows the hour, with no shadow.
You slide the pinhole to the month first.
Some rings are engraved with the latitudes where they work best.
Shakespeare may mention one in As You Like It, from 1599.
